questions.question: What invariant should a multimodal request preserve when images are tiled and packed into a language-model context?
options: The visual tokens retain media and spatial identity while the complete request stays inside its budget
Every image always receives the same token count
Text tokens can be discarded to make room for images
The model never needs metadata after decoding
questions.explanation: A flexible visual pipeline must preserve where evidence came from, while enforcing a bounded multimodal context and serving budget.

questions.question: A task needs to read tiny text across four document pages, but the request exceeds the context budget. What is the most defensible first response?
options: Silently drop two pages
Increase concurrency until the request fits
Apply an explicit resize, tiling, or page-selection policy and report the evidence limit
Remove all output-token reserve
questions.explanation: The product should make the transformation visible and preserve enough text and generation budget to complete the task. Silent evidence loss produces unsupported answers.

questions.question: Why can an aggressively pooled visual projector be risky for GUI grounding?
options: It automatically causes a network outage
It can discard the region-level detail needed to bind an instruction to a small control
It increases image resolution
It guarantees a longer context window
questions.explanation: Pooling can reduce token pressure, but it may remove the fine local structure needed for OCR, pointers, and precise controls.

questions.question: A vision worker is unavailable. When is a text-only fallback appropriate?
options: For every request, without telling the user
Only when a safe subset of the task can be completed without visual verification and the missing modality is explicit
Only after retrying the worker forever
Whenever a benchmark score is high
questions.explanation: A fallback must match the product contract. Tasks that need visual inspection should defer rather than imply that missing visual evidence was checked.

questions.question: Which signal best helps an operator explain why multimodal p95 latency increased?
options: Only the number of deployed services
Visual-token count, context utilization, queue wait, and per-stage latency
The model name alone
Average latency from last month
questions.explanation: The request budget and stage timings expose whether the change comes from input packing, queuing, the vision path, or decode work.

questions.question: What can a reported vision-language benchmark score establish by itself?
options: That a product is reliable for every production task
That a checkpoint achieved a result under the named dataset and protocol
That autonomous GUI actions are safe
That memory and latency SLOs will be met
questions.explanation: Benchmark evidence is scoped to its evaluation setup. Product quality also requires task-owned grounding, reliability, safety, and serving evaluation.
